headline: High: open-webui can ingest and act on content from shared files/MCP while awesome-prompts is a prompt source, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP, plugins, tools, and file inputs, so it can ingest attacker-controlled prompt text; awesome-prompts is a prompt repository that can supply such text. With no provenance tracking or isolation shown, the pair creates a direct instruction-hijack path. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF open-webui loads prompts or files from awesome-prompts without provenance filtering
IF an MCP/tool/plugin path passes repository text into the model context
mitigations: Disable automatic import of external prompt libraries
Require provenance labels on all imported prompt text
Restrict MCP/tools to allowlisted sources only
Review any prompt file before use
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, documents, notes, API keys, and persistent memory, and can use broad network egress; awesome-prompts is a prompt-writing source with no data-handling surface. If shared files or mounted volumes contain sensitive material, open-webui can transmit it to third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured with a shared workspace containing secrets or documents
IF an enabled API/tool path sends file contents to an external model or service
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared volumes
Disable external API connectors for sensitive workspaces
Use a separate workspace for prompt libraries
Audit outbound tool destinations
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while open-webui supports persistent shared sessions, files, and mounted volumes. There is no direct write-write conflict with the prompt repo, but open-webui can mutate shared state that may be consumed alongside prompt content. Uncertainty is limited by the lack of write capability in agent_a.
conditions: IF open-webui instances share the same mounted volume or Redis-backed session state
IF prompt files are edited in the same workspace as mutable app artifacts
mitigations: Separate prompt repositories from mutable app state
Use per-instance volumes
Disable shared sessions for sensitive deployments
Lock shared files during edits
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can treat imported content as context and then execute tools or present outputs; awesome-prompts supplies prompt text that may be treated as authoritative instructions. Without a verification step, bad prompt content can cascade into tool use or user-facing actions. The pair creates a default dangerous path because B is action-capable and A is instruction-bearing.
conditions: IF open-webui uses prompt-library content as system or developer instructions
IF tool-enabled chats act on model output without human review
mitigations: Mark imported prompts as untrusted
Require human approval before tool execution
Disable subprocess-capable tools for prompt-driven chats
Add output verification for tool calls
requires-engineering: implement policy checks before actions

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, files, documents, notes, and persistent memory, while awesome-prompts is a public prompt repository. If regulated data is placed into open-webui and then routed through external APIs, residency and retention obligations can be violated. Only open-webui is cited because the compliance risk is driven by its handling and egress surfaces; agent_a has no comparable data surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui
IF external API connectors or analytics are enabled for that data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Disable analytics and external connectors
Use local-only inference mode
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
